ledger.summary: Hardened the ledger economy (owned paths only; no commit). (1) The list is now `LedgerState.requests`, replacing `purchases`: PurchaseRecord | RefusalRecord keyed by (playerId, requestId). Only insufficient-gold, tonic-limit, player-in-duel and player-disconnected are kept; they charge nothing and replay with the same state even when they would now succeed. At most 16 per player (MAX_RECORDED_REFUSALS), oldest evicted, and an evicted id is decided afresh. PurchaseResult gains `refusal`. (2) addPlayer lost its `gold` option: every purse is rules.startingGold. checkLedger asserts goldIssued = players x startingGold + sum(grants), as well as balances + goldSpent = goldIssued. (3) Grant keys are bounded: ruin = String(island) of a source's island; supply-cache must be in the new `supplyCaches` (createLedger option, validated by the new content validateSupplyCaches, stored in state). Other keys are refused as unknown-source, and checkLedger flags unknown recorded keys. (4) The property test relaxes the same-state check only for a first-time kept refusal, which may change only requests and tick (checked by hash). It uses per-player request ids, adds rebuy misuse with the same player's own id for the other item, retries refusals, and asserts that no successful useTonic had an active tonic just before. It adds EXERCISED entries. (5) New scripted tests: shared ids, refusal replay after a grant, stale/unknown/left requests not kept, 17th refusal evicts the first, unknown keys including a fresh key per call, the minting invariant, and duel choosing-window refusals for purchase and useTonic. Changed test expectations: purchase refusal test ids renamed (r4/r5 reuse would now replay); another player's same id now succeeds instead of `duplicate`; ruin keys changed from 'ruin-N' to island strings, and a ruin with key 'supply-1' is now unknown-source; the PvP-rounding test sets startingGold in rules; the addPlayer gold:-1 check now asserts that a forged purse is ignored; the corrupted-state test uses the new shapes. docs/objectives.md updated (state, idempotency, invariant, economy, rumor flow). Checks run locally after npm ci: npm run typecheck, test:unit (679 passed), test:integration (36 passed), build: all exit 0.
open_assumptions: The property test keeps the old join-purse dice draw (discarded) so the seeded match sequence is unchanged. Without it, slice seeds stopped exercising 'contested completion fails'.
Property purses vary per seed through rules.startingGold (50/20/90).
A retry of a kept (player, id) for the other item is `duplicate` (not kept), as before.
A kept refusal advances state.tick, like any applied request.

findings.message: checkLedger only lightly validates the shape of the new request records (packages/simulation/src/objectives/invariant.ts economyProblems). Any outcome whose kind is not "purchase" falls into the refusal branch, even an unknown kind. For a refusal, only `rejection` is checked: not its `item`, not that its tick is at most state.tick, and not a non-empty requestId. `state.supplyCaches` is assumed to be an array, so a corrupted non-array value makes checkLedger throw instead of reporting a problem. The operations never produce such states, so this is hardening of the checker, not an exploit path.
findings.requirement: Keep one list of request outcomes keyed by (playerId, requestId), each either a purchase or a refusal with its rejection.

findings.message: The 'no supply caches' rule is tested only with an explicit empty list: ledger.test.ts 'only mints for keys the ledger knows' builds `new Run("alpha", ["a"], 11, undefined, [])`, which passes `supplyCaches: []`. No test creates a ledger with the option left out and then asserts `state.supplyCaches` is [] or that a supply-cache grant is refused. So the `createLedger` -> `createLedgerFromAssignment(..., supplyCaches = [])` default path (state.ts) is never checked. The ledgers at ledger.test.ts:143, 276 and 420 leave the option out but never test a supply-cache grant.
findings.requirement: a new optional `supplyCaches` list in `createLedger`; none means no supply-cache grants

findings.message: In property.test.ts the `rebuy` branch (around lines 336-347) makes assertions only when `result.replayed` is true, and even then it checks only that `purchase ?? refusal` is the original record, not that `ok` and `rejection` match it. If a kept (player, id) is retried for the same item and wrongly decided afresh (not replayed, `original` still present), the step is only counted (e.g. `rebuy:ok`) and nothing fails. The EXERCISED entry `refusal-replayed` catches only a total loss of replay. The scripted tests in ledger.test.ts ('replays a decided refusal, even once it would succeed…', 'keys request ids per player…') do assert this behaviour, so it is covered, but the randomised check does not enforce it.
findings.requirement: A retry of a recorded (playerId, requestId) returns the original result, refusal or success, with the very same state, even if it would succeed now.

# Decisions: ledger-economy-fixes

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24/25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- ledger-economy-001 was approved by both reviewers and is on `main` (`f31fa51`). Their P2s are exploit paths for real money, so they are fixed now, while nothing uses the economy yet. The work builds on `main` (branch `econ/fixes-base`), without a snapshot restore.
- Request ids are per player, and refusals replay: true idempotency, so a delayed retry never buys something the player gave up on.
- The invariant reconciles `goldIssued` with the recorded purses and grants, so minting outside the rules is caught by `checkLedger`, not just prevented by code structure.
- Grant keys are bounded by what the ledger knows (islands; supply-cache ids given at creation), so a careless caller can't mint.

- Corrected after design challenge attempt 1 (its alternative, adopted):
  - Only decided refusals are recorded (short gold, tonic limit, in a duel, disconnected); malformed, stale and unknown-player requests keep the same-state rule. At most 16 recorded refusals per player.
  - No caller-chosen purses at all.
  - Ruin keys are `String(island)`, and supply-cache ids live in the state.

## Assumptions

- Tests needing other purses set `startingGold` in the ledger's rules.

## Deferred

- Wiring into the room: `objectives-endgame`.

concerns.message: The scripted-test harness `Run.do` (ledger.test.ts:74-81) asserts `expect(state).toBe(before)` for every rejection, not just the property test's. Recorded refusals (insufficient-gold, tonic-limit, player-in-duel, player-disconnected) now change the state, so every existing scripted purchase-refusal test fails in the harness. The task only mentions relaxing the property test. The doc on `LedgerRejection` in internal.ts:11-14 also says a rejected request 'always returns the very state object it was given'.
concerns.consequence: The worker may drop the same-state assertion from `Run.do` entirely, which silently loses the §16 same-state guarantee for every other operation. Or the existing tests fail until it is narrowed. The relaxation should match the property test's exactly: only a first-time refusal with one of the four recorded reasons. The internal.ts doc also needs updating, and the report should list which expectations changed.

concerns.message: Removing caller-chosen purses means deleting `gold: dice.percent(20) ? dice.int(400) : undefined` from the property test's `join` action (property.test.ts:180). That removes a draw from the main `dice` stream, so every 1200-step sequence for seeds 1-3 changes. The EXERCISED table is seed-specific coverage. Rare entries such as 'late return', 'leaving during a choice window' and 'third tonic' (which now needs 90 gold from grants, since everyone starts on 50) can disappear. The grant keys also change, from `ruin-n`/`supply-n` to `String(island)` and declared cache ids.
concerns.consequence: The coverage assertion fails for reasons unrelated to correctness, and the worker spends time re-tuning weights or seeds. Keeping a discarded `dice.percent(20)` draw at that spot keeps the match sequence as it is.

concerns.message: The plan doesn't say whether recording a refusal advances `state.tick` (`atTick`). The tick is documented as 'the latest world tick an applied request carried', and a refusal is not applied. It also doesn't say whether `checkLedger` bounds a refusal's `tick` by `state.tick`, the way it already bounds `tonicEffect.startTick`.
concerns.consequence: Different choices give different state hashes and staleness behaviour. If a refusal advances the clock, a refused purchase can make other same-batch requests carrying earlier ticks stale. If it doesn't, the record can hold a tick later than `state.tick`. Either way the choice should be deliberate, asserted in `checkLedger` and documented in docs/objectives.md.

concerns.message: `checkLedger` is only required to exclude refusals from the `goldSpent` sum. It isn't required to check the refusal records themselves: at most 16 per player; rejection limited to the four recorded reasons; a known player; (playerId, requestId) unique across purchases and refusals; no price. The property test also isn't required to check that a first-time recorded refusal changed nothing except the outcome list.
concerns.consequence: The 16-refusal bound and the 'refusal charges nothing' rule would be enforced only by the code's structure. decisions.md rejects exactly that for minting. A bug that decremented tonics, or kept a 17th refusal, on a refusal would pass every check, because the gold equation doesn't cover tonics or list length.

concerns.message: `supplyCaches` is added only to `createLedger`. `createLedgerFromAssignment` (the restore path) also builds a `LedgerState` and needs the list, plus validation: unique, non-empty strings. Nothing in content or in any other package defines supply-cache ids yet, so this feature invents their format.
concerns.consequence: A ledger restored from a match record would silently refuse every supply-cache grant as `unknown-source`. Duplicate or empty ids in the list would make the 'one global claim per cache' rule ambiguous. objectives-endgame will also have to supply ids in whatever format is chosen here, so the format should be documented.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Leave `purchases` and `PurchaseRecord` exactly as they are, and add one bounded `refusals` list next to them: `{ playerId, requestId, item, rejection, tick }`, at most 16 per player, oldest evicted first. Change the replay lookup in `purchase()` to search both lists by (playerId, requestId). This meets every acceptance item: a single lookup keyed by (playerId, requestId), refusals and successes both replaying, and refusals excluded from `goldSpent` by construction. It also avoids reshaping the purchase record, the `goldSpent` sum, docs, and the existing tests that read `state.purchases` (ledger.test.ts:182, 706). If the 'one list' wording in the acceptance is taken literally, a discriminated union in one array works too, as long as purchases keep their current fields and `goldSpent` sums only the `purchase` entries.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before any refactor, make three edits to property.test.ts: drop the `gold:` option from `join` but keep a discarded `dice.percent(20)` draw in its place; change the grant keys to `String(shop.int(islands))` and a declared supply-cache pool; change the `rebuy` misuse to the same player with a different item. Then run `npm run test:unit -- property`. This takes a few minutes. It shows whether the EXERCISED coverage for seeds 1-3 survives fixed 50-gold purses and bounded keys, especially 'third tonic', 'short gold' and 'rebuy:duplicate'. If it doesn't, adjust the weights or add a targeted scripted test before building the refusal machinery on top.

# Task: ledger

## Goal

Harden the ledger economy that ledger-economy-001 added (now on `main`, approved by both reviewers) against the exploit paths its reviewers found. Money must be impossible to mint, double-spend or grief, even through a careless caller.

## Context

- Read `features/ledger-economy/ledger-task.md` and `decisions.md` (all still applies), `docs/objectives.md` ("Economy"), and `packages/simulation/src/objectives` (`economy.ts`, `invariant.ts`, `players.ts`, and the tests: `ledger.test.ts`, `property.test.ts`).
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Other features run at the same time and own the sea, server, web and tests, plus `packages/*/src/intel`. Stay inside your owned paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Keep the structure, names and patterns, and every existing test except where this task changes an expectation (say which in your report).

## Acceptance

Each item names the test that proves it.

1. **Per-player request ids.** Purchases are keyed by (playerId, requestId), so one player's id can never refuse or reveal another's purchase. Scripted test: two players use the same id and both succeed. Each one's retry replays their own result.
2. **Decided refusals replay too.** Keep one list of request outcomes keyed by (playerId, requestId), each either a purchase or a refusal with its rejection.
   - **Recorded:** only refusals that are decisions on a well-formed request from a known player at a current tick: `insufficient-gold`, `tonic-limit`, `player-in-duel`, `player-disconnected`. A recorded refusal charges nothing and is excluded from the `goldSpent` sum.
   - **Not recorded:** malformed, stale, unknown-player and left-player requests keep the documented same-state rule (§16).
   - A retry of a recorded (playerId, requestId) returns the original result, refusal or success, with the very same state, even if it would succeed now.
   - **Bounded:** at most 16 recorded refusals per player. The oldest is evicted first, and an evicted id is evaluated fresh if retried (documented).
   - Relax the property test's "a rejected step changes nothing" check only for a first-time recorded refusal. Adapt its `rebuy` misuse to repeat the same player's own id.
   - Update `docs/objectives.md`: the idempotency section, and the rumor flow, where `replayed` can now come with `ok: false`.
   - Scripted tests: a purchase refused for short gold, retried after a grant, still returns `insufficient-gold`, and a new id then succeeds; a stale or unknown-player request returns the same state; the 17th refusal evicts the first.
3. **The minting invariant.** Every purse equals `state.rules.startingGold`, with no caller-chosen purse and no test-only option; tests that need other purses create the ledger with `rules: { ...objectiveRules, startingGold: n }`. The ledger records every grant. `checkLedger` asserts that `goldIssued` equals players × `startingGold` plus the sum of grants, and that `balances + goldSpent = goldIssued`. Scripted test: a state with `goldIssued` and a balance both raised outside `grantGold` fails `checkLedger`.
4. **Bounded grant keys.**
   - A `ruin` grant's key is exactly `String(island)` for one of the ledger's islands (known from its sources), matching the ruins module's key.
   - A `supply-cache` grant's key must be one of the supply-cache ids given at ledger creation (a new optional `supplyCaches` list in `createLedger`; none means no supply-cache grants). The list is stored in `LedgerState`, so `hashState` covers it, and `checkLedger` rejects any recorded grant whose key isn't a known island or supply cache.
   - Unknown keys are refused as `unknown-source`.
   - Scripted tests for both, including a fresh unknown key per call failing every time.
5. **Sharper checks.**
   - The property checker asserts, per step, that a successful `useTonic` found no active tonic for that player in the prior state, so stacking would fail.
   - Scripted tests refuse purchases and `useTonic` in the duel's `choosing` window as well as `fighting`.
6. `npm ci` then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build` pass from a clean checkout.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After sixty minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

# Decisions: ledger-economy-fixes

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24/25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- ledger-economy-001 was approved by both reviewers and is on `main` (`f31fa51`). Their P2s are exploit paths for real money, so they are fixed now, while nothing uses the economy yet. The work builds on `main` (branch `econ/fixes-base`), without a snapshot restore.
- Request ids are per player, and refusals replay: true idempotency, so a delayed retry never buys something the player gave up on.
- The invariant reconciles `goldIssued` with the recorded purses and grants, so minting outside the rules is caught by `checkLedger`, not just prevented by code structure.
- Grant keys are bounded by what the ledger knows (islands; supply-cache ids given at creation), so a careless caller can't mint.

- Corrected after design challenge attempt 1 (its alternative, adopted):
  - Only decided refusals are recorded (short gold, tonic limit, in a duel, disconnected); malformed, stale and unknown-player requests keep the same-state rule. At most 16 recorded refusals per player.
  - No caller-chosen purses at all.
  - Ruin keys are `String(island)`, and supply-cache ids live in the state.

## Assumptions

- Tests needing other purses set `startingGold` in the ledger's rules.

completion.summary: Hardened the ledger economy (owned paths only; no commit). (1) The list is now `LedgerState.requests`, replacing `purchases`: PurchaseRecord | RefusalRecord keyed by (playerId, requestId). Only insufficient-gold, tonic-limit, player-in-duel and player-disconnected are kept; they charge nothing and replay with the same state even when they would now succeed. At most 16 per player (MAX_RECORDED_REFUSALS), oldest evicted, and an evicted id is decided afresh. PurchaseResult gains `refusal`. (2) addPlayer lost its `gold` option: every purse is rules.startingGold. checkLedger asserts goldIssued = players x startingGold + sum(grants), as well as balances + goldSpent = goldIssued. (3) Grant keys are bounded: ruin = String(island) of a source's island; supply-cache must be in the new `supplyCaches` (createLedger option, validated by the new content validateSupplyCaches, stored in state). Other keys are refused as unknown-source, and checkLedger flags unknown recorded keys. (4) The property test relaxes the same-state check only for a first-time kept refusal, which may change only requests and tick (checked by hash). It uses per-player request ids, adds rebuy misuse with the same player's own id for the other item, retries refusals, and asserts that no successful useTonic had an active tonic just before. It adds EXERCISED entries. (5) New scripted tests: shared ids, refusal replay after a grant, stale/unknown/left requests not kept, 17th refusal evicts the first, unknown keys including a fresh key per call, the minting invariant, and duel choosing-window refusals for purchase and useTonic. Changed test expectations: purchase refusal test ids renamed (r4/r5 reuse would now replay); another player's same id now succeeds instead of `duplicate`; ruin keys changed from 'ruin-N' to island strings, and a ruin with key 'supply-1' is now unknown-source; the PvP-rounding test sets startingGold in rules; the addPlayer gold:-1 check now asserts that a forged purse is ignored; the corrupted-state test uses the new shapes. docs/objectives.md updated (state, idempotency, invariant, economy, rumor flow).
